Objective
Learn to recognize and solve a quadratic equation with exactly one distinct real solution. The root occurs twice algebraically, but represents only one x-value.
Repeated root
The equation x squared minus six x plus nine equals zero factors into x minus three squared. The only real root is x equals three.
Discriminant
For a x squared plus b x plus c equals zero, compute D equals b squared minus four a c. Exactly one real solution means D equals zero.
Why the formula agrees
The quadratic formula is negative b plus or minus square root D, divided by two a. When D is zero, both signs produce the same root.
Worked example
For x squared minus eight x plus sixteen equals zero, D equals sixty four minus sixty four, or zero. The repeated root is four.
Factoring check
The same equation is x minus four squared equals zero. Substitute x equals four to verify sixteen minus thirty two plus sixteen equals zero.
Unknown middle coefficient
If x squared plus k x plus sixteen has one real solution, set k squared minus sixty four equal to zero. Both k equals eight and k equals negative eight work.
Unknown constant
For two x squared minus twelve x plus c, set one hundred forty four minus eight c equal to zero. The answer is c equals eighteen.
Graph meaning
A quadratic with one repeated real root touches the x-axis at its vertex and turns around. It does not cross the axis at two different points.
Desmos strategy
Enter y equals x squared minus eight x plus sixteen. Look for the single x-axis touch at four. The discriminant is faster for exact parameter questions.
Common exam traps
Do not confuse D equals zero with D greater than zero. If a parameter is squared, check both positive and negative branches and keep a nonzero.
Recap and next steps
Write the equation in standard form. Set b squared minus four a c equal to zero. Solve for the unknown and verify the repeated root using negative b divided by two a.
